prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Production enemy sprite for Depths, a dark stressful first-person pixel dungeon crawler. Silhouette-led restrained pixel art, large crisp clusters, at most three broad shades per material, warm upper-left highlights and dark cool shadows. Flat sparse surfaces, no individual fur, veins smaller than a large readable mark, no pores/grain/noise, no gradients/dithering/antialiasing, no glossy rendering, no ground shadow, background or text. Serious and unsettling, not cute/cartoon. Front-facing full-body transparent square canvas; keep all anatomy/equipment inside with generous 10% margins. Designed to reduce to a native128x128 sprite with max32 shared colours, bottom-centre scene origin (64,120). No scenery or UI. A goblin brute, one head taller and twice as broad as a common lean goblin. Same long pointed ears, ochre-olive skin, angular toothy goblin face, rough brown leather/cloth kit and rusty iron. Huge stooped shoulders, short neck, squat powerful legs. Crude iron rectangular maul with a simple wooden haft, both hands loosely gripping it low at one side; no buckler or knife, no helmet/crown. One idle pose, full body front-facing and planted feet. Menace from weight and posture, simple shapes. Reference goblin supplies race, palette and pixel simplicity only; replace the narrow body, knife and buckler with the much broader brute body and maul described.
